excludes: Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by design-system-implement: Implement or bootstrap design tokens, accessible primitives, component variants, theming, documentation, and adoption tooling in a frontend stack

Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by frontend-architecture: Design frontend application architecture including component hierarchies, state management, routing, data fetching, form systems, and build strategies
native_ownership.responsibility: Design read-only token, component, theming, governance, distribution, and adoption contracts from product, design, accessibility, and repository evidence

risk.rationale: The contract requires explicit repository and runtime safety evidence; mutation authority remains limited to the user's requested scope.

negative.prompt: The primary requested outcome is: Implement or bootstrap design tokens, accessible primitives, component variants, theming, documentation, and adoption tooling in a frontend stack. Follow the existing repository conventions.

Please produce this deliverable: Design frontend application architecture including component hierarchies, state management, routing, data fetching, form systems, and build strategies. Verify the affected behavior.

positive.prompt: Design a read-only design-system architecture from existing product, brand, accessibility, token, component, platform, ownership, and adoption evidence; compare alternatives without implementing it.
Decide token layers, component contracts, governance, distribution and phased adoption for a multi-brand product, deriving scales and abstractions from evidence rather than fixed recipes.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the answer within design-system-architecture's stated responsibility and does not recreate native Codex orchestration.

Uses the supplied fixture as authoritative repository context, may re-check that evidence during execution, and does not invent file contents, package-manager commands, or exact paths that the fixture does not provide.
Uses an ordered, risk-driven workflow rather than a static checklist and does not bypass material missing evidence, incompatible capability, failed validation, or unsafe authority.

Establishes authoritative sources and ownership, derives token and component contracts from product/platform evidence, treats accessibility criteria with level and exception nuance, rejects fixed scales and two-use abstraction thresholds, and separates architecture from implementation or migration.

Grounds verification in the applicable authoritative categories supplied by the selected fixture; relevant domain-specific subchecks may refine those categories. Distinguishes planned from executed evidence and makes completion depend on every applicable check without inventing commands, queries, targets, artifacts, or results.

Reports enough hypothetical repository context to ground the decisions or proposed changes, not-yet-executed checks and expected acceptance evidence, residual risks, and unresolved external boundaries without inventing results.
Keeps optional provider or version detail subordinate and loads a linked reference only when needed; does not expand into a neighboring skill's primary ownership.

scenarios.prompt: An existing multi-brand product has undocumented values, repeated exceptions, one installed component primitive, and conflicting design files. A stakeholder mandates a 4px scale, 44px AA targets, and extraction after two uses. Produce an evidence-based architecture instead.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the deliverable read-only and requires source-of-truth ownership, consumer inventory, representative pilot, compatibility checks, migration sequencing, deprecation, verification and rollback before implementation.
Rejects remembered tool syntax and universal token, taxonomy, target-size or abstraction recipes; distinguishes observed product evidence, explicit policy, and unresolved design decisions.
Defines rendered-state, accessibility, contract, visual-regression and consumer adoption evidence for a pilot; generating tokens or Storybook successfully is not system adoption proof.
Does not invent a framework version or version-gated API when the task provides no release context.

scenarios.prompt: A team wants to replace production tokens and primitives immediately based on a remembered Storybook/Tailwind recipe, with no inventory, consumer compatibility map, owner, pilot, or rollback. Define the safe read-only architecture boundary.

assertions.criterion: Uses installed manifests, lockfiles, runtime files and capability evidence for an existing project; treats an upgrade as a separate migration.

Checks the cross-stack compatibility dimensions applicable to the selected repository, such as engine, peers, compiler/framework, test runner, or deployment runtime, without demanding irrelevant dimensions.

For any version-sensitive command or API selected from repository evidence, verifies it with an applicable capability source such as installed/generated types, CLI help, configuration schema, or matching official documentation. When the fixture cannot identify a concrete command/API, states the exact evidence required and does not invent one.

scenarios.prompt: Use design-system-architecture in an existing project whose manifests and lockfiles pin an older supported release. A newer stable release also exists. Choose compatible guidance without silently upgrading.

assertions.criterion: Resolves stable or LTS release data at execution time from the configured official sources, checks cross-stack compatibility, and lets the generated manifest and lockfile become authority.

scenarios.prompt: Start a greenfield project that needs design-system-architecture. No manifest or lockfile exists yet. Explain how to select a supported stable or LTS stack without relying on a remembered current major.
